faq.a: Tap 'Start Your Transformation', share your goal and details, and our coach will contact you on WhatsApp for a free consultation.

faq.q: Are the diet plans vegetarian friendly?
faq.a: Yes. Every plan is available in vegetarian and non-vegetarian versions and uses everyday Indian food.

faq.q: What is the difference between free and paid diet plans?
faq.a: The free plan gives you calorie and macro targets with a sample day. The paid plan is made by a coach around your body, routine, budget, food choices and health notes, with revisions and support.

faq.q: Do I need to go to a gym?
faq.a: No, we design both home workouts (with minimal or no equipment) and gym-based workout routines based on your preference.

faq.q: How often will coach Shivam check my progress?
faq.a: You get weekly formal check-ins with body measurements and weight review, along with ongoing daily WhatsApp support for form and diet queries.

blog.title: 5 Habits That Make Fat Loss Actually Last
body: Fat loss is not about a 30-day crash diet. It is about habits you can repeat on a busy Tuesday. Start with a modest calorie deficit, 8,000 to 10,000 steps a day and a protein source in every meal.
Sleep 7 to 8 hours, drink enough water and weigh yourself at the same time each week. Judge progress by the weekly average, not by one day on the scale.

blog.title: Indian Diet for Muscle Gain: Simple and Budget Friendly
body: You do not need expensive imported food to build muscle. Dal, paneer, curd, eggs, soya, chana, milk and rice cover most needs when portions are planned.
Aim for around 1.6 to 2 g of protein per kg of body weight, spread across 4 to 5 meals, and eat a little above your maintenance calories.

blog.title: Home Workout Plan: No Equipment Needed
body: Push-ups, squats, lunges, planks and glute bridges can build a strong base at home. Train 4 days a week and add reps or slow down the tempo each week.
Progressive overload still applies at home. If a set feels easy, make the movement harder instead of just doing more of it.

blog.title: Why Motivation Fails and Discipline Wins
body: Motivation comes and goes. A system carries you through the days you do not feel like training. Lay out your clothes, book your slots and track every session.
Aim to never miss twice. One skipped workout is a blip, two in a row starts a new habit.
